articles.title: DSA Scores Election Victories Across California: From San Diego to Humboldt, membership gains fuel increased activism and wins
articles.author: California DSA
articles.content_excerpt: The returns are (mostly) in, and DSA-endorsed candidates for elected offices from local school boards to the U.S. Congress have been elevated throughout California. A ton of hard work went into this critical election cycle, boosted on the one hand by DSA’s swelling membership, which is now numerically the largest of any socialist organization in the country’s history, and on the other hand by the understanding that in order to stop the march of fascism we had to win big. A half dozen cities in the Golden State are now led by DSA mayors, including the largest one. DSA has become a recognized political force, drawing praise from our coalition allies and dismay from our opponents. articles.title: L.A. Socialists Turn Electoral Wave into Governing Power
articles.author: California DSA
articles.content_excerpt: LA Mayor-elect Nithya Raman “LA was at a critical cusp in its history. Globalization had reorganized its economy, rewiring it in dramatic ways, and many people were being left behind. Yet the city had—and still has—this incredible, protean potential for better things, for progressive politics, for surprising activism.” – Mike Davis The midterm elections were truly seismic. Like many places across the country, Los Angeles made good on its protean potential from the 2026 blowout with a stronger socialist movement and a larger share of political power. DSA members won up and down the ballot. Nithya Raman has famously won the mayor’s office of the country’s second largest city in a upset victory. Marissa Roy has won the city attorney’s office, and Angela Gonzales-Torres is headed to Congress.

articles.title: California DSA’s “Tax the Rich Campaign”: one for two
articles.author: California DSA
articles.content_excerpt: Don’t throw away your pitchforks. You will have more chances to use them in the near future. With the loss of Proposition 40, the Billionaire Tax, by a slim statewide margin of 52.1–47.9%, California DSA’s 2026 “Tax the Rich” campaign went one for two. The other progressive tax on the ballot, Proposition 3, the Education and Health Care Act, won handily, 61-39%. Any attempt to spin the SEIU/United Health Workers-backed Prop 40 defeat as an indicator that California’s electorate doesn’t want to tax the rich—billionaires included—is either uninformed or deliberately misleading. articles.title: Protect members’ retirement funds and invest in a clean and safe future for our children
articles.author: California DSA
articles.content_excerpt: CalSTRS (California State Teachers’ Retirement System) is the world’s largest educator-only public pension fund, delivering reliable returns to investors while managing billions of dollars of assets. Teachers rely on their pensions to be invested responsibly: both with fiduciary responsibility and divesting from companies that contribute to genocide, apartheid, and environmental destruction. It is great that CalSTRS has formally acknowledged the need for a policy to mitigate environmental, social, and governance risks with investments. However, the current policy offers no enforcement mechanism to ensure teachers’ valued retirement funds are invested responsibly. articles.content_excerpt: Comrades on May Day 2026. Photo by Bonnie Lockhart They say history doesn’t repeat itself, but it rhymes. That’s certainly the case in Oakland these days with the return of a proposed coal depot. articles.title: Star Trek and our Socialist Horizon
articles.author: California DSA
articles.content_excerpt: Last month Sir Patrick Stewart passed away after battling Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia. Stewart had a long and accomplished career, but to many of us his most iconic role was that of Jean Luc Picard, captain of the U.S.S. Enterprise on Star Trek: The Next Generation . The series, spanning almost 200 episodes, took us across time and space, and the character of Jean Luc Picard navigated perilous situations as his crew explored the galaxy. There can be much said about Stewart as a comrade , but what I want to convey to you is how Star Trek , and science fiction as a whole, can invigorate our socialist imagination as in our theory and practice we boldly go where no one has gone before. articles.title: Let’s Make a Better Democratic Party in California
articles.author: California DSA
articles.content_excerpt: At the February 2026 California Democratic Party (CDP) convention, a caucus of about 100 delegates from Sacramento area congressional District 7 failed by two votes to deny out of touch corporate Democrat and longtime incumbent Representative Doris Matsui the party endorsement outright and force a vote of the full Central Committee. Before the vote, Nancy Pelosi and several other House members entered the room in what was at least a breach of propriety. The caucus chair felt obliged to invite Pelosi to say a few words, which morphed into a lengthy endorsement of Matsui—clearly intimidating a few delegates whose votes tipped the scale. articles.title: Amazon Workers Have Won a First North American Contract
articles.author: Adam D. K. King
articles.content_excerpt: Amazon has spent years and enormous resources trying to prevent its North American workforce from unionizing. Even where workers have successfully organized, the retail giant has used everything from legal challenges to warehouse closures to frustrate their efforts to secure a first contract. Now, for the first time, workers at an Amazon facility in North America have a collective agreement. On November 13, an independent arbitrator issued a three-year contract covering approximately eight hundred workers at Amazon’s YVR2 fulfillment center in Delta, British Columbia, a suburb of Vancouver. The workers are represented by Unifor Local 114, part of Canada’s largest private sector union. The agreement represents an important breakthrough in the struggle to organize Amazon. articles.title: Rediscovering Rosa Luxemburg’s History of Ancient Rome
articles.author: Serena Unzueta
articles.content_excerpt: More than a century after her death, Rosa Luxemburg is renowned as a revolutionary socialist and leader of the 1919 Spartacist Uprising in Germany. Her writings have long been a touchstone for socialist theory. But her work as an ancient historian remains almost entirely unknown. Luxemburg’s political writings, especially her work on political economy, were full of historical references, and indeed she often stressed the importance of history to the project of political economy — and revolution itself — in her major works. These references offered a tantalizing glimpse into a rich archive of study on Luxemburg’s part, but there was a frustrating lack of further elaboration on historical topics and the study of history itself. articles.title: I Play Rocky Is Undeniably Charming
articles.author: Eileen Jones
articles.content_excerpt: I Play Rocky goes for earnest meathead sentimentality in the most shameless way, which is presumably why it’s undeniably a crowd-pleaser. It makes Song Sung Blue (2025 ) — another heartwarming underdog story of working-class American dreamers making good against all odds — look like the height of sophistication. But whereas Song Sung Blue was about delightfully “Midwest nice” characters wearing sequined outfits in a Neil Diamond tribute band who find unlikely fame, I Play Rocky is the semi-fictionalized story of how Sylvester Stallone got Rocky made. The sleeper hit of 1976, Rocky was produced on a shoestring budget, spawned a zillion-dollar Hollywood franchise, and made Sylvester Stallone an overnight star. articles.title: The US-Israel Relationship Is Shifting. Not Nearly Enough.
articles.author: Gilbert Achcar
articles.content_excerpt: On November 3, the very day of the midterm congressional elections, Donald Trump announced that the United States would cease its annual military aid to Israel at the end of this year. That aid, amounting to $3.8 billion annually, was provided under an agreement signed by the Obama administration in 2016, covering the ten years from 2019 through 2028. Trump cannot end it on his own — the money is appropriated by Congress — but the announcement was no surprise: it had been signaled before, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, now leading a caretaker government after Israel’s October election, said he was fine with it (or pretended to be), arguing that the Zionist state no longer needs this money and is perfectly capable of purchasing US weapons at its own expense. articles.title: Black Political Power Rising
articles.author: Erin Aubry Kaplan
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. The ultimate meaning of the midterms is still unfolding, but one thing’s for sure: It was a hell of a moment for Black representation. After all the obstacles the GOP threw in the path of Black voting in the South, from stringent voter ID laws to stacked election boards, when the dust had settled the seemingly impossible had happened: Black women had won multiple statewide seats in Georgia, including governor; five Black people were elected governor, a historic high; and Scott Colom took a Senate seat in Mississippi, the first time a Black man has been elected senator in Mississippi since Reconstruction.
